display_title: HORIZON-CL5-2026-11-D3-04 De-risking renewable fuel technologies through transnational pre-commercial procurement of renewable fuel industrial value chains – Horizon Europe
call_module_title: HORIZON-CL5-2026-11-D3-04 De-risking renewable fuel technologies through transnational pre-commercial procurement of renewable fuel industrial value chains
executive_summary: A Horizon Europe pre-commercial procurement action (the EU co-funds a transnational group of buyers that jointly procures competing R&D from several suppliers) to de-risk and bring industrial value chains of essential renewable fuel technologies, such as advanced biofuels for aviation and e-methanol or biomethane for shipping, to TRL 8. Consortia need at least three independent legal entities from three countries, at least two of them public procurers from different Member States or Associated Countries; expected procurers include airport and port authorities, aircraft operators and shipping companies. The topic budget is EUR 40 million for around one project, funded at up to 100%. Single-stage; opened 4 August 2026, deadline 1 December 2026 at 17:00 Brussels time.
status_rationale: Climate, Energy and Mobility Work Programme 2026-2027 (Part 8), pp. 120–122, Specific conditions, Expected Outcome and Scope, funds a buyers' group of fuel users (for example airport and port authorities, aircraft operators and shipping companies) that procures R&D to bring renewable fuel value chains for aviation and shipping to TRL 8, with hydrogen as an end product out of scope. It does not touch TenneT's electricity-transmission field: no project file is close to it, the procurement need is for fuels TenneT does not buy, and the topic sets no task concerning grids, system operation or electricity markets.
